newsitem.title: UK: London freight - Market remains in owners favour.
newsitem.headline: London freight - Market remains in owners favour.

text.p: London, March 13 (reuter) - Apart from sluggish trading in the north Atlantic, the freight market has continued to move in the owners' favour, brokers said.
Caper and panamax rates were stronger in the Indian ocean and Far East with a number of charterers involved in period timecharters of panamax tonnage.
The Baltic Freight Index (BFI) was up 11 points to 1,465, whie modern handymax rates improved generally lifting the Baltic Handy Index gained 15 points to 1,100.
The BIFFEX futures ended five to 22 points easier. volume totalled 264 lots. April traded last at 1,598. down 22.

Gin T.K. Boesen was reported to have booked Andre tonnage for 54,000 heavy grain U.S. Gulf/Japan for April 15/30 at $26.25 combo, although there were conflicting reports about whether the no combo rate was $25.50 or $25.75. Last fixed for April 1/15, was Evagelistra at $24.50 no combo.
Cargill was reported to have covered 85,000 grains U.S. Gulf/Egypt with a caper vessel for March/April at $13.00
Although delays up to 35/40 days were said to be experienced by vessels in Paranagua, prompt fixtures were completed from this port with Birlad to Lisbon by Andre of 50,000 tonnes at close to $14.50.
Another, was Hunter to Barcelona by Marifran with 55,000 tonnes at $16.50, both lumpsum equivalents basis heavy grain.
Dreyfus quoted an unusual fresh enquiry of 40/45,000 soybeans for spot shipment from Brazil to New Orleans, following Glencore's recent enquiry for tonnage for a similar cargo to USEC for April 1/20.
No news emerged about Safmarine's rumoured fixture of a Panamax plate/Far East but Daiichi were linked with the NYK-relet Bunga Srigading 65,921 dwt for the same trip on private terms.
Two handy-size Plate/Venezuela stems were thought fixed.
One was, 20,000 tonnes on Katerina K by unknown charterers, and 25,000 tonnes on a Lauritzen vessel by Interbulk, but full details were not forthcoming.
Andre was working a 25,000 tonne corn stem up river Plate/Cape Town for March 20/28 at $20.50/20.75, and was said to have covered 26,000 wheat Rouen/Port Sudan for March loading.
Groupe Pantin was linked with Dover 23,000 dwt delivery prompt north France trip Red Sea with bagged wheat products at $10,000 daily.
In the U.S. Gulf, Dreyfus booked a prompt vessel of 750,000 cubic feet U.S. Gulf/Ireland at close to $20.00.

CAM paid a firmer $23.00 for 25,000 wheat U.S. Gulf/Algeria with the 1974-built Pontoporos for end March/early April basis 1,500 discharge, and cargill was said to be willing to concede $24.00 in this trade, basis 2,000 discharge.
MINERALS - The Atlantic remained difficult for owners with early tonnage, but firm in the East.

Thalassini Avra 129,237 dwt prompt Passero was believed fixed privately, and the 1981-built Mercedes 133,000 dwt, failed on subjects with Pan Ocean for 2-4 months at $10,500 daily, was believed to have gone on subjects to Docenave delivery Antwerp March 17/27 for two laden legs Atlantic trading at over $11,000.
Taiwan Power booked three coal cargoes of 120,000 tonnes each to Kaohsiung for April and May, from Newcastle at $6.78, Long Beach at $8.83, and Richards Bay at $8.59.
In addition to this, they fixed three cargoes of 55,000 tonnes from U.S. Gulf to Taiwan for May shipment at between $19.64 and $20.40.
Halla was said to have taken Capitano Giovanni 74,500 dwt from mid April in Mizushima for six to eight months at $12,000.
Anangel Progress 69,400 dwt was said still on subjects with European charterers for a around six to eigth months basis delivery Taiwan end March at close to $12,000 daily.
The 1981-built Western Trade 65,083 dwt was fixed by Yukong in direct continuation delivery prompt Japan for four to six months at $10,000 daily.
Maratha Mighty 72,870 dwt was thought fixed prompt Japan on subjects for period business.

Trip business was fixed by Belships with the 1976-built Oetker-relet C.Tahsin 66,041 dwt delivery Richards Bay end March trip Milaki at $8,500 daily plus $120,000 bonus, illustrating the firm conditions in the Indian ocean.
HANDY-SIZES - Most areas were said to be active, although few fixtures were reported.

In the Far East, Wadi al Natroon 45,115 dwt was said to have been taken by Korea Line delivery Philippines end March for three months at about $8,800 daily, and Dunaj 33,230 dwt open prompt Port Keelang was understood to have fixed an Australian round at close to $8,500 daily.
